children: TELA Bio’s third-quarter revenue declined 8% year over year, while its net loss widened 8%. Lower OviTex PRS sales and U.S. price-mix headwinds drove the revenue decline; a higher inventory obsolescence charge and increased interest expense contributed to the larger loss, partly offset by lower operating expenses.
¹ Reported as “Revenue”. ² Reported as “Net loss”. ³ Reported as “Net loss per common share, basic and diluted”.
: OviTex sales volume fell 1% to 5,757 units; OviTex PRS volume declined 29% to 946 units.
: Fell to 65% from 68%, reflecting a higher excess and obsolete inventory charge, including a $1.0M write-off of expired inventory.
: Sales and marketing expenses decreased 14% and research and development expenses fell 32%, primarily due to lower compensation costs.
: The August plan reduced headcount by approximately 20%; the company reported $1.7M in severance expense for the quarter.
: TELA Bio received 510(k) clearance in September for Liora, its fully resorbable surgical mesh device.
